note: A dollar-denominated universe, because every KRX allocation result topped out at 8% a year while simply holding the NASDAQ returned 22%: asset choice dominated every rule tested. History starts in 2005 rather than 1985 because the defensive funds a balanced book needs did not exist earlier — TLT lists in 2002, GLD in 2004 — so the dot-com bust is out of reach here even though the leverage study could reach it.
currency_warning: Everything here is priced in USD and a Korean investor also carries KRW/USD. That is not modelled. It generally helps: the dollar rises when Korean equity falls, measured at -0.533 correlation against KOSPI 200, so a won-based investor's real drawdown on these funds is smaller than the numbers below.
tax_warning: Gains on US funds are taxed as 해외주식 양도소득세 (22% above the annual allowance), unlike a domestic ETF. A rule that trades more realises more, and none of that is modelled.
cost_note: Prices are Yahoo's adjusted series, so distributions are included and each fund's own fee is already deducted from its net asset value. Do not add --expense-ratio on top of that; it would be charged twice.
